newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-CARLING RETIRES FROM INTERNATIONAL SIDE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CARLING RETIRES FROM INTERNATIONAL SIDE.

text.p: Will Carling, who captained England a record 59 times, said on Sunday he was quitting international rugby.

Carling announced his decision in his regular column for the Mail on Sunday newspaper. "I said that I would make no announcement until the beginning of next season but I see no reason now to prolong the inevitable," he said.

At 22 the youngest England captain for 50 years when he was appointed in 1988, Carling stepped down at the end of the 1996 season but still retained his place at centre for the recent Five Nations matches.
During Carling's time as captain, England won 44 and drew one of their 59 matches. Altogether he played 72 internationals.
"If I believed I could get to the next World Cup in two years then there would be a goal to carry on and try to win it but, realistically, I do not feel I can do that," said Carling.
"I had something I wanted to prove this year -- that I could earn my place as a player, not as a captain -- but I cannot find a reason like that for playing on next year."
